paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2013 - Verifiable private multi-party computation Ranging and ranking
title: Verifiable Private Multi-party Computation: Ranging and Ranking
motivation: Existing MPC protocols assume honest participation but neglect verifiability; malicious parties can forge inputs or lie about results.
problem_framing: Define verifiable private multi-party computation where parties compute functions on private inputs without revelation, and no malicious party can cheat others to accept incorrect results.
key_insight: Two attacks discovered on existing schemes: (1) compressive sensing enables reconstructing sparse vectors from O(K log M) dot products; (2) homomorphic signatures allow fake signature generation. Solution: use certificates from trusted authority to bind encrypted values.
method_signature: Threshold-based ranging and ranking protocols using Paillier encryption with certificates from trusted third party; both input and outcome verifiable.
evaluation_criteria: Computation time and communication cost on laptop and mobile phone; practical efficiency measured as less than 0.5s for most protocols.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: P1 can launch binary search by adjusting threshold θ to narrow down value range of f(v1,v2); suggests threshold from system or query time limit.
evidence_for_taste: verifiability of user inputs and outcomes are neglected
malicious adversary may simply forge his/her input value
a party P_i is able to generate a fake signature
Protocol 4 is unconditionally verifiable when at most one party cheats
when P1 and P2 collude, they can cheat the aggregator
thinking_moves: Identify overlooked attack surface in existing privacy-preserving MPC
